title: chore: assorted cleanup across modules
body:
This PR rolls up a handful of small maintenance items that have been accumulating across the codebase. None of these are intended to change product behavior in a meaningful way; the focus is on consistency, reducing noise, and smoothing out a few rough edges that came up while reviewing adjacent code paths.

Included in this sweep:

- fix a couple of outdated wording/typo issues in `README.md` to align with current terminology
- normalize some inline comments in `htdocs/include/common.php` for readability and consistency with surrounding code
- remove an unused helper import in `htdocs/libraries/icms/view/theme/Object.php`
- simplify a small bit of request-to-object handling in `htdocs/libraries/icms/ipf/Controller.php` to better match the rest of the controller flow
- rewrap a long docblock in `htdocs/kernel/module.php` so it follows the prevailing formatting used elsewhere
- tidy whitespace and trailing blank lines in `htdocs/class/pagenav.php`
- reorder a few constant declarations in `htdocs/include/version.php` to keep related values grouped together
- clean up a stale comment in `htdocs/modules/system/admin/preferences/main.php` that no longer reflects the current code path

This is primarily housekeeping, but bundling these together should make subsequent functional changes easier to review by reducing incidental diff noise in nearby files.

# ImpressCMS

ImpressCMS is a community developed Content Management System. With this tool maintaining the content of a website becomes as easy as writing a word document. ImpressCMS is the ideal tool for a wide range of users: from business to community users, from large enterprises to people who want a simple, easy to use blogging tool. ImpressCMS is a powerful system that gets outstanding results and it is free!

Starting with the 1.4 branch of ImpressCMS, we are also fully compatible with PHP 7.x.

### What can you do with it?

ImpressCMS can be used for many types of web sites. The system is highly scalable and it can be used for example as an intranet for a company with 20,000 employees as well as for building a simple 5-page website for the promotion of your company. 
The system is extremely useful for managing online communities because it has the ability to create user groups and assign permissions for managing content to each different group.

For each type of website ImpressCMS offers different functionality with a collection of free modules that are available on [https://www.impresscms.org/modules/downloads/](https://www.impresscms.org/modules/downloads/). A few examples of what you can do with them:

* Publish news of your organization
* Let visitors contact you through a state of the art customizable contact form
* Create and manage articles
* Add a forum to your site
* Sell products through your web site using an online store
* ...and many more

### List of key features

#### :package: Fully modularized

Website content is managed by separate content modules/web applications. Simply install the module which has the features you need: a news module, forum module, photo album module, there are many many third party modules to choose from.

#### :earth_africa: Supported World-wide

ImpressCMS was created and is maintained by a team of hard-working volunteers working from all over the world. The ImpressCMS community has support sites around the world for support of non-English speaking users.

#### 🗃️ Database-driven

ImpressCMS uses a database to store the data required for running your ImpressCMS site. MySQL and MariaDB is currently supported. Support for other DBMS's is coming soon.

args.comment:
Declining this PR.

The PR description lists a small, targeted set of cleanups across ~8 files (README.md, common.php, pagenav.php, version.php, etc.), but the actual diff shows sweeping whitespace/line-ending churn across many third-party vendored files under `htdocs/editors/tinymce/jscripts/...` and `htdocs/libraries/smarty/...`. Files like `about.js`, `anchor.js`, `resource.db.php`, and `modifier.debug_print_var.php` appear to have every single line removed and re-added with no textual change — this is almost certainly a newline-style (LF ↔ CRLF) or trailing-whitespace conversion.

Problems with landing this as-is:

1. **Misleading description.** The scope described ("tidy whitespace and trailing blank lines in pagenav.php", etc.) does not match reality. Reviewers should be able to trust the PR body.
2. **Vendored code should not be touched.** Reformatting third-party TinyMCE/Smarty sources makes future upstream updates and diffs significantly harder to apply and review, and destroys `git blame` history on those files for no functional benefit.
3. **Bundled with legitimate changes.** The genuinely useful cleanups (README typo fixes, docblock rewrap in `kernel/module.php`, constant reordering in `include/version.php`, etc.) are drowned in tens of thousands of no-op line changes, making the PR effectively unreviewable.

Please split this up:
- One PR for the actual code cleanups listed in the description.
- If a line-ending normalization is truly desired, do it in a dedicated PR, scoped to first-party code only (exclude `htdocs/editors/tinymce/**` and `htdocs/libraries/smarty/**`), and ideally accompanied by a `.gitattributes` update so it doesn't immediately regress.

Happy to re-review once the scope matches the description.

# ImpressCMS

ImpressCMS is a community developed Content Management System. With this tool maintaining the content of a website becomes as easy as writing a word document. * Sell products through your web site using an online store
* ...and many more

# ImpressCMS

ImpressCMS is a community developed Content Management System. With this tool maintaining the content of a website becomes as easy as writing a word document. * Publish news of your organization

* Create and manage articles

* Sell products through your web site using an online store
* ...and many more

# ImpressCMS

ImpressCMS is a community developed Content Management System. With this tool maintaining the content of a website becomes as easy as writing a word document. * Sell products through your web site using an online store

# ImpressCMS

ImpressCMS is a community developed Content Management System. With this tool maintaining the content of a website becomes as easy as writing a word document. ImpressCMS is the ideal tool for a wide range of users: from business to community users, from large enterprises to people who want a simple, easy to use blogging tool. ImpressCMS is a powerful system that gets outstanding results and it is free!

Starting with the 1.4 branch of ImpressCMS, we are also fully compatible with PHP 7.x.

### What can you do with it?

ImpressCMS can be used for many types of web sites. The system is highly scalable and it can be used for example as an intranet for a company with 20,000 employees as well as for building a simple 5-page website for the promotion of your company. 
The system is extremely useful for managing online communities because it has the ability to create user groups and assign permissions for managing content to each different group.

For each type of website ImpressCMS offers different functionality with a collection of free modules that are available on [https://www.impresscms.org/modules/downloads/](https://www.impresscms.org/modules/downloads/). A few examples of what you can do with them:

* Publish news of your organization
* Let visitors contact you through a state of the art customizable contact form
* Create and manage articles
* Add a forum to your site
* Sell products through your web site using an online store
* ...and many more

### List of key features

#### :package: Fully modularized

Website content is managed by separate content modules/web applications. Simply install the module which has the features you need: a news module, forum module, photo album module, there are many many third party modules to choose from.

#### :earth_africa: Supported World-wide

ImpressCMS was created and is maintained by a team of hard-working volunteers working from all over the world. The ImpressCMS community has support sites around the world for support of non-English speaking users.

#### 🗃️ Database-driven

ImpressCMS uses a database to store the data required for running your ImpressCMS site. MySQL and MariaDB is currently supported. Support for other DBMS's is coming soon.
